guide.summary: Forgejo documents OAuth2 Authorization Code (with PKCE) for third-party apps acting for the connected user on a customer's own instance. OAuth2 scopes are not implemented, so the token can act for the user within that user's existing access.
guide.recommendation: The requested access is documented. Follow the saved setup steps and run each representative API test; execution has not been verified.

findings.title: OAuth2 Authorization Code grant with PKCE is documented for Forgejo
findings.detail: Forgejo acts as an OAuth2 provider with user consent. It supports the Authorization Code grant with PKCE, and the documented authorization and access-token endpoints are under /login/oauth.
findings.appliesWhen: Customer connects an individual account on their own Forgejo instance using OAuth

evidence.quote: Supported OAuth2 Grants At the moment, Forgejo only supports the Authorization Code Grant standard with additional support for the following extensions:
Authorization Endpoint /login/oauth/authorize Access Token Endpoint /login/oauth/access_token
Proof Key for Code Exchange (PKCE)

findings.title: OAuth2 tokens are not scoped and can perform any action for the user
findings.detail: Scopes are not implemented for OAuth2 tokens, which can be used to execute any actions on behalf of the user. The documented token boundary is therefore the connected user's access, and the app must stay read-only by its own behavior.
findings.appliesWhen: Applies to the OAuth token used for the connected person

evidence.quote: Note Scopes are not implemented for OAuth2 tokens and they can be used to
execute any actions on behalf of the user, not just Git-related actions.
OAuth2 scopes are not yet implemented.

findings.title: Customer registers the OAuth2 application in their own user settings
findings.detail: An OAuth2 application must be registered in the user settings applications page, with a confidential or public client type and a redirect URI. The client ID and secret are then used in the token exchange.
findings.appliesWhen: Each customer instance where the app is connected

evidence.quote: OpenID Connect (OIDC) To use the Authorization Code Grant as a third-party application, it is required to register a new application via the “Settings” ( /user/settings/applications ) section. To test

It is possible for any user to manually register a new OAuth2 application on the /user/settings/applications page for the purpose of using Git credential helpers different from the pre-registered ones.
Client types Forgejo supports both confidential and public client types, as defined by RFC 6749 .

findings.title: Instance-wide admin-created OAuth apps grant administrative rights
findings.detail: Third-party applications obtaining a token through an instance-wide OAuth2 application have administrative rights. Customer-registered user applications are a separate path.
findings.appliesWhen: Applies only if the app is created as an instance-wide application on /admin/applications rather than by a customer in user settings

evidence.quote: Note Third-party applications obtaining a token for a user via such an application will have administrative rights.
Forgejo can act as an instance-wide OAuth2 provider. To achieve that, OAuth2 applications must be created on the /admin/applications page.

It is possible for any user to manually register a new OAuth2 application on the /user/settings/applications page for the purpose of using Git credential helpers different from the pre-registered ones.

steps.title: Register the OAuth2 application on the customer instance
steps.detail: Customer creates an OAuth2 application at their instance /user/settings/applications page using a public client with PKCE and a redirect URI they control. Record the client ID. Because OAuth2 tokens are unscoped, the app must enforce read-only behavior itself.
steps.doneWhen: The customer has a client ID and a redirect URI registered for the connected instance; no secret is used for the public client.

evidence.quote: OpenID Connect (OIDC) To use the Authorization Code Grant as a third-party application, it is required to register a new application via the “Settings” ( /user/settings/applications ) section. To test
Client types Forgejo supports both confidential and public client types, as defined by RFC 6749 .
For public clients, a redirect URI of a loopback IP address such as http://127.0.0.1/ allows any port. Avoid using localhost , as recommended by RFC 8252 .

fields: INSTANCE_BASE_URL: customer-provided full HTTPS origin of their Forgejo instance
REDIRECT_URI: developer-chosen callback registered for the app

steps.title: Open the consent redirect and verify the callback
steps.detail: Send the customer to the documented authorization endpoint with PKCE parameters. The customer approves access; the app checks that the returned state matches the value it generated before exchanging the code.
steps.doneWhen: The browser returns to REDIRECT_URI with a code and the same state value that the app generated.

evidence.quote: Redirect the user to the authorization endpoint in order to get their consent for accessing the resources:

https://[ YOUR-FORGEJO-URL ]/login/oauth/authorize?client_id=CLIENT_ID&redirect_uri=REDIRECT_URI&response_type=code&code_challenge_method=CODE_CHALLENGE_METHOD&code_challenge=CODE_CHALLENGE&state=STATE The CLIENT_ID can be obtained by registering an
The user will now be asked to authorize your application. If they authorize it, the user will be redirected to the REDIRECT_URL , for example:

fields: CODE_CHALLENGE: S256 hash of a 43-128 character code_verifier generated by the app
STATE: random value generated by the app and compared on callback
INSTANCE_BASE_URL: your full HTTPS instance URL, without a trailing slash

steps.title: Exchange the authorization code for an access token
steps.detail: The app posts the returned code and its code_verifier to the documented token endpoint as a public client, without a client secret.
steps.doneWhen: The token response contains an access_token with token_type bearer.

evidence.quote: POST https://[YOUR-FORGEJO-URL]/login/oauth/access_token { "client_id" : "YOUR_CLIENT_ID" ,
"code" : "RETURNED_CODE" ,

Response: { "access_token" : "eyJhbGciOiJIUzUxMiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJnbnQiOjIsInR0IjowLCJleHAiOjE1NTUxNzk5MTIsImlhdCI6MTU1NTE3NjMxMn0.0-iFsAwBtxuckA0sNZ6QpBQmywVPz129u75vOM7wPJecw5wqGyBkmstfJHAjEOqrAf_V5Z-1QYeCh_Cz4RiKug" ,

fields: RETURNED_CODE: taken from the callback query string, provided by the consent step
CODE_VERIFIER: the app-generated verifier matching the code_challenge
INSTANCE_BASE_URL: your full HTTPS instance URL, without a trailing slash

steps.title: List visible repositories, first page
steps.detail: Request the first page of repository search with private=true, the documented default that includes private repositories the user can access. Use limit=50, the documented maximum page size on this instance. Each entry's repository name is read from the data array at $.data[].name. Join the name of every entry in data, not only the first. The OAuth access token is sent as a Bearer token, which is accepted for this endpoint.
steps.doneWhen: The response has ok true and a data array. Each entry's name is read from data[].name. Boundary check: confirm the token came from the OAuth code exchange and the outgoing request log contains only GET requests to /api/v1/repos/search, with no create, edit or delete calls.

evidence.quote: Operation security: [{"BasicAuth":[]},{"AuthorizationHeaderToken":[]},{"SudoParam":[]},{"SudoHeader":[]},{"TOTPHeader":[]}] Successful response 200: SearchResults
Parameter private in query (boolean, optional): include private repositories this user has access to (defaults to true)
"max_response_items" : 50, "default_paging_num" : 30,

fields: ACCESS_TOKEN: OAuth access_token from the exchange-code response; user-specific, keep it out of the guide
INSTANCE_BASE_URL: your full HTTPS instance URL, without a trailing slash

steps.title: Confirm read-only behavior and private visibility boundary
steps.detail: Nonmutating check: confirm the first-page response includes only repositories the connected user can see, and confirm the app issues no POST, PUT, PATCH or DELETE calls. Do not create, edit or delete repositories to test this.
steps.doneWhen: Inspected request log shows only GET requests to listing endpoints and visible results match the connected user's access.

evidence.quote: write : POST , PUT , PATCH , and DELETE routes (in addition to GET )
All (public, private, and limited)
All public repositories are accessible, but access is limited to read-only APIs if the public repository is not included in the specified repositories.

steps.title: Request the remaining pages of visible repositories
steps.detail: Continue from the first page. If the response Link header contains rel next, follow that next URL unchanged with the same Bearer token. Do not build cursors yourself. The documented page and limit parameters drive pagination, and the example shows page=2 for the first continuation. Repeat until the Link header has no rel next. The x-total-count header gives the total number of items, so the names collected across all pages should match it.
steps.doneWhen: Pagination ends only when the Link header has no rel next, and the names collected across all pages match x-total-count. Boundary check: confirm the token came from the OAuth code exchange and the outgoing request log contains only GET requests to /api/v1/repos/search, with no create, edit or delete calls.

evidence.quote: Pagination The API supports pagination. The page and limit parameters are used to specify the page number and the number of items per page. As well, the Link header is
returned with the next, previous, and last page links if there are more than one page. The x-total-count is also returned to indicate the total number of items.
< link: < https://forgejo.example.org/api/v1/repos/search ? limit = 1 &page = 2 > ; rel = "next", < https://forgejo.example.org/api/v1/repos/search? limit = 1 &page = 5252 > ; rel = "last"

fields: page: increment from the previous request if not following the Link next URL
next Link URL: the rel next value from the previous response, followed unchanged
ACCESS_TOKEN: OAuth access_token from the exchange-code response; user-specific, keep it out of the guide
INSTANCE_BASE_URL: your full HTTPS instance URL, without a trailing slash

coverage.action: List repository names visible to the connected person, including pagination
coverage.reason: OAuth2 scopes are not implemented, so the token acts as the connected user with no named scope. Read-only use is checked through the outgoing request log. Third-party OAuth applications have administrative rights, so the grant is broader than the listing needs. Use it only for this read-only listing.

evidence.quote: OAuth2 scopes are not yet implemented.

Use the access_token to make API requests to access the user’s resources.

details.title: OAuth2 Authorization Code grant with PKCE is documented for Forgejo
details.detail: Forgejo acts as an OAuth2 provider with user consent. It supports the Authorization Code grant with PKCE, and the documented authorization and access-token endpoints are under /login/oauth.
details.appliesWhen: Customer connects an individual account on their own Forgejo instance using OAuth

evidence.quote: Supported OAuth2 Grants At the moment, Forgejo only supports the Authorization Code Grant standard with additional support for the following extensions:
Authorization Endpoint /login/oauth/authorize Access Token Endpoint /login/oauth/access_token
Proof Key for Code Exchange (PKCE)

details.title: OAuth2 tokens are not scoped and can perform any action for the user
details.detail: Scopes are not implemented for OAuth2 tokens, which can be used to execute any actions on behalf of the user. The documented token boundary is therefore the connected user's access, and the app must stay read-only by its own behavior.
details.appliesWhen: Applies to the OAuth token used for the connected person

evidence.quote: Note Scopes are not implemented for OAuth2 tokens and they can be used to
execute any actions on behalf of the user, not just Git-related actions.
OAuth2 scopes are not yet implemented.

details.title: Instance-wide admin-created OAuth apps grant administrative rights
details.detail: Third-party applications obtaining a token through an instance-wide OAuth2 application have administrative rights. Customer-registered user applications are a separate path.
details.appliesWhen: Applies only if the app is created as an instance-wide application on /admin/applications rather than by a customer in user settings

evidence.quote: Note Third-party applications obtaining a token for a user via such an application will have administrative rights.
Forgejo can act as an instance-wide OAuth2 provider. To achieve that, OAuth2 applications must be created on the /admin/applications page.

It is possible for any user to manually register a new OAuth2 application on the /user/settings/applications page for the purpose of using Git credential helpers different from the pre-registered ones.

preparation.title: Registration worksheet
preparation.text:
Register the OAuth2 application on the customer instance
Customer creates an OAuth2 application at their instance /user/settings/applications page using a public client with PKCE and a redirect URI they control. Record the client ID. Because OAuth2 tokens are unscoped, the app must enforce read-only behavior itself.
Fields: INSTANCE_BASE_URL: customer-provided full HTTPS origin of their Forgejo instance, REDIRECT_URI: developer-chosen callback registered for the app

preparation.title: First connection test
preparation.text:
Open the consent redirect and verify the callback
Done when: The browser returns to REDIRECT_URI with a code and the same state value that the app generated.

Exchange the authorization code for an access token
Done when: The token response contains an access_token with token_type bearer.

List visible repositories, first page
Done when: The response has ok true and a data array. Each entry's name is read from data[].name. Boundary check: confirm the token came from the OAuth code exchange and the outgoing request log contains only GET requests to /api/v1/repos/search, with no create, edit or delete calls.

Confirm read-only behavior and private visibility boundary
Done when: Inspected request log shows only GET requests to listing endpoints and visible results match the connected user's access.

Request the remaining pages of visible repositories
Done when: Pagination ends only when the Link header has no rel next, and the names collected across all pages match x-total-count. Boundary check: confirm the token came from the OAuth code exchange and the outgoing request log contains only GET requests to /api/v1/repos/search, with no create, edit or delete calls.
